arrival: From Liverpool Lime Street the ground is around two miles away; the club says a taxi from the city centre is usually £8-£10. The 917 Express bus runs from Commutation Row (near Lime Street) in about 15 minutes, and routes 26 (Liverpool ONE), 17 (Queen Square), 68/168, 14 and 19 also stop nearby; a matchday 926 service starts 3.5 hours before kick-off from Liverpool ONE. By Merseyrail, go to Sandhills and take the Soccerbus, which runs from 2 hours before kick-off. Kirkdale is the closest station (just under a mile); Stanley Park car park is permit holders only.
from_airport: Liverpool John Lennon Airport: shuttle bus to Liverpool South Parkway, then Merseyrail Northern Line to Sandhills and the Soccerbus, or a taxi of 20-30 minutes depending on traffic. From Manchester Airport, take a direct train or coach to Liverpool city centre then bus or rail to Anfield.
away_end: Visiting fans are in the Anfield Road Stand (allocation around 3000 for league games) with licensed safe standing in rows 6-35. Enter via gates Q and R, approaching Anfield Road from the 97 Avenue direction; there is no access from Arkles Lane. Turnstiles open 2 hours before kick-off.
meeting: The club guide names no pubs. Football Ground Guide names The Arkles (77 Anfield Road) as the main pub for travelling fans a few minutes from the ground, plus The Flat Iron (Walton Breck Road) and The Thomas Frost Wetherspoons (Walton Road), and says many visiting fans drink in the city centre around Concert Square, Bold Street or Mathew Street before heading to the ground.
bags: Only small handheld bags no larger than A5 (148.5 x 210mm) are allowed and all bags get a visual search; larger bags are only permitted for medication or medical equipment with prior approval via disability@liverpoolfc.com at least 48 hours before the game. Banned items include cans, flasks, glass, plastic bottles over 500ml, laptops or tablets, drones, selfie sticks, flares, tools, weapons, laser devices, musical instruments and loud hailers; no bag storage is offered by the club.
after: The 927 bus departs St Domingo Road (by the Valley Sports Bar) for 2.5 hours after the match, the 917 returns from Walton Lane, and the Soccerbus to Sandhills runs for 90 minutes after full-time. Expect long queues for the Soccerbus and busy bus stops, with Walton Breck Road closed to traffic as the crowd leaves; coaches leaving turn left. Last trains to Manchester: not stated.
tips: Anfield is fully cashless (contactless or chip-and-PIN). Everyone is searched and pyro detection dogs may be present, so arrive early; fans without tickets are urged not to travel. Alcohol is served on the visiting concourse but cannot be consumed in view of the pitch, and the ground is no-smoking including e-cigarettes. Ticket collection: not stated (Ticket Office is under the Kop).

arrival: Newcastle Central Station is a ten-minute walk: head west along Neville Street then turn right onto St James' Boulevard and the stadium is at the top. Monument Metro station is a five-minute walk and St James Metro station is right by the ground. Haymarket and Eldon Square bus stations are on Percy Street, five minutes away; the nearest taxi rank is two minutes away opposite the Chinatown entrance, with major ranks at Central Station. There is no public parking at the stadium; a Park and Ride (X50, £2 return) runs from the Metrocentre and drops off on Barrack Road.
from_airport: Newcastle International Airport has its own Metro station; the club guide says the Metro to the city centre (Haymarket, Monument or Central) takes about 25 minutes with trains up to every 12 minutes in daytime, and Monument is a five-minute walk from the ground.
away_end: Away fans are on Level 7 of the Leazes Stand (the Leazes End, top tier), reached by 140 steps and 14 landings with a lift available on request from a steward. Use turnstiles 89-94 in the Leazes Stand (normally 91-94) according to the access number on your ticket; turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off and step-free access is near turnstiles 93-94.
meeting: The club says there is no designated away pub and some nearby venues may refuse visiting supporters, particularly in colours, but Shearer's Bar under the Gallowgate Stand is open to all supporters and The Gate and Chinatown are a short walk away. Football Ground Guide names The Head of Steam and The Newcastle Tap (Neville Street, by Central Station), Percy Arms (Percy Street), The Trent House (Leazes Lane), and says The Strawberry near the ground generally admits away fans.
bags: Bags larger than A4 (the prohibited items list gives 10x20x30cm) are not permitted and there is no bag storage at the stadium; medical exemptions must be arranged in advance via accessibility@nufc.co.uk and no exemption is given for travel or accommodation reasons. Banned items include glass, canned drinks, weapons, pyrotechnics, smoke canisters, air horns, lasers, drums, flag poles, prams and video recording equipment; all bags and people are searched.
after: Strawberry Place and Leazes Terrace close from two hours before kick-off until roughly 30-45 minutes after full time, and Barrack Road closes 10 minutes before full time for 20-45 minutes, so allow extra time. Central Station is a ten-minute walk and Monument Metro five minutes; the Metrocentre Park and Ride returns from St James' Boulevard with the last bus one hour after the final whistle. Last trains to Manchester or London: not stated.
tips: Away Ticket Office is beside turnstiles 91/92, open from 1.5 hours before kick-off; download digital tickets before arriving and charge your phone. Contactless is encouraged at kiosks, with cash accepted only at a limited number of locations. The Level 7 concourse sells burgers, pies, hot and cold drinks with vegetarian and halal options; alcohol is sold before kick-off and at half-time.

arrival: Selhurst, Thornton Heath and Norwood Junction stations are each about a 15-minute walk from the ground; do not use Crystal Palace station, which is two miles away. The club gives total journey times of about 40 minutes from Victoria (Southern to Selhurst), 30 minutes from London Bridge (Southern to Norwood Junction), 45 minutes from Waterloo via Clapham Junction, and 50 minutes from Euston or King's Cross via the Northern line to London Bridge. Taxis should drop off at the corner of Park Road and Whitehorse Lane at the visiting supporter end; there is no parking at the stadium and surrounding streets are permit holders only.
from_airport: Gatwick is the practical airport: a direct train runs to Norwood Junction, or a taxi of 30-40 minutes. From Heathrow, take the Heathrow Express or Piccadilly line into London and connect to Selhurst, Thornton Heath or Norwood Junction (taxi 45-60 minutes).
away_end: Visiting supporters are in the corner of the Arthur Wait Stand next to the Whitehorse Lane end (around 2000 places); the away turnstiles are on one side of the Arthur Wait Stand and away fans usually use entrances 4, 5, 6 or 7. Turnstiles open around two hours before kick-off.
meeting: The club page names no pubs. Football Ground Guide names The Prince George (2 High Street, Thornton Heath) as the most popular, about a 10-minute walk, plus The Railway Telegraph (Brigstock Road, Thornton Heath), The Clifton Arms (Clifton Road, SE25) and The White Horse (Selhurst Road, SE25).
bags: A bag or backpack is allowed if it is small enough to fit under your seat, subject to a full search at the turnstiles; larger luggage can be left free of charge at the Information Centre by Entrance 9, open three hours before kick-off until 30 minutes after the final whistle. Banned items include knives, fireworks, smoke canisters, air horns, flares, weapons, laser devices, bottles, glass, cans, poles and drones; only soft drinks under one litre in factory-sealed plastic bottles may be brought in, no alcohol.
after: Roads around the stadium close from three hours before kick-off until about one hour after the final whistle, and the ground is residential so keep noise down when leaving. Return via Norwood Junction (London Bridge), Selhurst (Victoria) or Thornton Heath (London Bridge or Clapham Junction); expect plenty of trains to London Bridge but a long wait for Clapham Junction services and a cramped away concourse. Last trains to Manchester: not stated; the N68 night bus serves evening matches.
tips: Selhurst Park is cashless (Apple Pay and Google Pay accepted). Visiting tickets are collected at Entrance 4; the Box Office closes two hours before kick-off. Views from the very back of the Arthur Wait Stand are poor, so arrive early; the concourse sells burgers, pies, chips and alcohol before kick-off and at half-time.

arrival: Arsenal (Piccadilly line) is the nearest station, about three minutes' walk, but has no step-free access; Finsbury Park (Victoria and Piccadilly lines, Great Northern rail) and Highbury & Islington (Victoria line, Mildmay line, Great Northern rail) are each about a 10-minute walk. From King's Cross take the Piccadilly line to Arsenal or the Victoria line to Highbury & Islington. Holloway Road is exit-only before matches and eastbound trains do not stop there; Drayton Park is closed on matchdays. Buses stop on Holloway Road, Nag's Head, Seven Sisters Road, Blackstock Road and Highbury Corner; the club strongly advises against driving as an Event Day Parking Scheme covers the area.
from_airport: From Heathrow take the Piccadilly line direct to Arsenal (about 1 hour 10 minutes); from Gatwick take a train to Victoria then the Victoria line to Highbury & Islington (about 1 hour 15 minutes); from Luton or Stansted take a train to King's Cross St Pancras then the Piccadilly line to Arsenal (about 1 hour).
away_end: Away fans are in the lower tier of the south-east corner, between the East Stand and the Clock End (just under 3000 for Premier League games). Enter via turnstiles K and L at the south-east corner; turnstiles open 120 minutes before kick-off and Arsenal recommends arriving at least 60 minutes before kick-off, using the Clock End Bridge from Arsenal station as it is quieter than the North Bank Bridge.
meeting: Arsenal's pages name no pubs. Football Ground Guide names the Drayton Park pub (formerly the Drayton Arms, opposite the large ARSENAL letters, often called the away pub), the Twelve Pins near Finsbury Park station (away fans sometimes welcome in small groups) and The Coronet Wetherspoons on Holloway Road, all within a 10-minute walk, and suggests drinking in central London before taking the tube.
bags: Only bags A4 size or smaller are allowed; large bags and suitcases are not permitted and all bags are searched and tagged, which slows entry. Arsenal points to luggage storage at London King's Cross station rather than offering any at the ground; flags and banners in the away end must be fire certificated.
after: Holloway Road station is closed for up to two hours after the match, so use Arsenal, Finsbury Park or Highbury & Islington, all with managed post-match queuing. Arsenal station queues can mean a wait of at least 30 minutes, so consider walking to Finsbury Park; the club advises arriving early and leaving later to avoid crowds. Last trains to Manchester: not stated.
tips: The stadium is cashless; the away end sells food and drink from two hours before afternoon games (6.30pm before evening games) with an Early Bird pie-and-pint offer up to 45 minutes before kick-off. Tickets are emailed as PDFs to scan on your phone; the Match Day Box Office is next to the Armoury store on the west side and opens 3 hours before kick-off. Buggies and prams are not allowed and under-14s must be with an adult.

arrival: The stadium is about 4 miles from Brighton city centre, so do not try to walk from Brighton station. Take a train from Brighton station to Falmer (about 7-10 minutes, roughly four trains an hour on matchdays); Falmer station is about 250m from the stadium and a short walk to the South Stand away end. Trains are very busy, so Brighton advise boarding around an hour before kick-off, or use Lewes (one stop beyond Falmer) as a quieter alternative. Bus 25 stops at Village Way (nearest stop) and bus 23 serves Falmer village and station; buses do not run from Brighton station itself. Your match ticket gives free train and bus travel in the Free Travel Zone from 3.5 hours before kick-off until 3.5 hours after the final whistle - fans from London only need a rail ticket as far as Haywards Heath.
from_airport: Gatwick is the nearest airport, under half an hour north of Brighton on the main London-Brighton line, with direct trains to Brighton station; from there take the Falmer train as above.
away_end: Away fans are in the South Stand (blocks S1A/S1B to S1F), about 600 yards from Falmer station. Away tickets are processed through Entrance 28 (turnstile gates 28-31 were used for visiting fans in May 2026); turnstiles open 2 hours before kick-off.
meeting: No pubs near the Amex are open to away fans - the Falmer pub is home-only and checks tickets. Away fans generally drink around Brighton station or in central Brighton (Yates and Wetherspoons are the usual suggestions) or in Lewes; there is a small fan zone with mobile bars outside the north-east corner and the North Stand bar is open to both sets of fans after the match.
bags: No bags larger than A4 (21cm x 29.7cm); all fans and bags are searched, with pyro and drug dogs. A bag drop for larger bags, suitcases and motorcycle helmets operates outside the South East / Village Way entrance - the fee is quoted variously as £5 (Jan 2026) and £7.50 (Mar 2026), and one Oct 2025 guide said there was no bag storage, so check before travelling. Flags need pre-approval from the South Stand Manager and a fire safety certificate.
after: Falmer station queues can take up to 50 minutes to clear and buses fill fast; the South Stand concourse stays open for an hour after the match and the North Stand bar is open to both sets of fans, so waiting is an option. Park & Ride buses run back up to 90 minutes after the game. Free rail travel covers journeys started within 3.5 hours of the final whistle; last-train times to London or Manchester: not stated.
tips: The Amex is fully cashless. Arrive early - the concourse opens 2 hours before kick-off and visiting fans are advised to arrive at least an hour before. Do not park on streets near the ground (residents' scheme, heavy ticketing); Park & Ride at Mill Road (fills about 1.5 hours before kick-off) or Brighton Racecourse must be pre-booked. Report anti-social behaviour by text to 07880 196442.

arrival: From Birmingham New Street take a local train (10-15 minutes, extra services on matchdays) to Witton, the nearest station to the away turnstiles - turn left out of the station, down to the roundabout, then left into Witton Lane for the away entrance a few minutes' walk away. Aston station is the alternative, about a 10-15 minute walk. Villa also run a matchday express city centre shuttle bus from Dudley Street (near New Street station) to Villa Park, open to home and away fans. Street parking around the ground is residents-only with £60 fines, and a traffic exclusion zone covers Witton Lane and Trinity Road from 2 hours before kick-off to 30-60 minutes after.
from_airport: Birmingham International Airport is the nearest; it is about 25 minutes by road (allow more for matchday traffic) or by train into Birmingham New Street and then a local train to Witton.
away_end: Away fans are in the north-east corner of the Doug Ellis Stand: Doug Ellis Lower Block Q (about 1600 seats) via turnstiles Q91-Q96B, and Doug Ellis Upper Block P (about 1300 seats) via turnstiles P87, P88, P88A and P89 (64 steps to the upper concourse). Turnstiles open about 90 minutes before kick-off; late arrivals can use Q96 and/or P89 until the second half starts.
meeting: Villa say there is no dedicated away pub or bar near the ground and advise drinking in Birmingham city centre. Football Ground Guide lists The Witton Arms (Witton Road), The Bartons Arms (High Street, Aston) and The Yew Tree (Brookvale Road) but warns some pubs check tickets.
bags: The official 2026/27 away guide says small bags are OK and will be searched, larger bags and luggage are not allowed and there is no storage, so avoid bringing a bag; Villa's own matchday pages say no bags larger than A4, all bags are searched and bags can be registered at villa.dropmybag.co.uk. Flags and banners need a photo emailed to the club at least 3 days before.
after: Witton station can have large queues after the match, with extra football services running to Birmingham New Street; the city centre shuttle bus also runs back to Dudley Street. Driving away can be slow (one reviewer reported about 90 minutes to rejoin the motorway). Last-train times: not stated.
tips: Villa Park is cashless (cash back available at the ticket office with a £3.50 minimum spend; nearest cash machine at Tesco Extra, Aston Lane). Have your ticket ready - barriers with ticket checks are sometimes used at the turnstiles. Alcohol is sold only in Doug Ellis Lower Block Q (none in Upper Block P, no transfers) and not at all for some fixtures - call 0333 323 1874 to check. Upper tier fans should buy programmes from the Witton Lane kiosks before entering. Uncollected tickets go to the visitors' ticket office on Witton Lane opposite the away coach park, open about 90 minutes before kick-off. Follow @WMPVillaFC for travel updates.

arrival: Kew Bridge is the nearest station (South Western Railway from London Waterloo, about every 15 minutes on matchday Saturdays, not step-free). Brentford station is the nearest step-free station, about 20 minutes' walk. Gunnersbury (District line and London Overground) is also close but has a small platform with restricted access at busy times; Kew Gardens, Chiswick Park, South Acton, Acton Town and South Ealing are other options - eight stations are within a 20-minute walk. Buses 65, 110, 237, 267, H91 and 391 serve the stadium. Taxis and Uber are available but expect longer waits after the match.
from_airport: Not stated by the sources. (Heathrow is the nearest; the Piccadilly line to Acton Town then the District line to Gunnersbury is the obvious route - unverified.)
away_end: Away fans are in the East Stand (blocks N120, E115-E117 and E215-E218). Use away entrances F, G or H off Capital Interchange Way; turnstile G is the accessible entrance via a lift from Thomas Layton Way. Turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off and there is no re-entry.
meeting: Pubs around the ground generally welcome both home and away fans. Brentford name The Gunnersbury and The Pilot near Gunnersbury station, Express Tavern, One Over the Ait, The Bell & Crown, The Steam Packet and City Barge closest to the stadium, and The Rose and Crown, The Greyhound, The Coach & Horses and The Botanist on Kew Green. Fulham Supporters Trust (Apr 2026) describe The Gunnersbury (590 Chiswick High Road) as the designated away pub and suggest booking.
bags: Brentford strongly recommend not bringing a bag; maximum size is 34cm x 24cm x 11cm, measured by stewards, with no folding to fit. Oversized bags, suitcases, prams and buggies can only be stored at the Bees Superstore (opens 2 hours before kick-off), £5 per item or £10 for the largest bags and suitcases, and must be collected by the time on your storage ticket. Prohibited items include alcohol, cans, glass or dark plastic bottles, water over 500ml, laptops and tablets, large cameras, air horns, flares and poles; small folding umbrellas and flags up to 2m x 1m are allowed.
after: Away fans are discouraged from using Kew Bridge after the match; if you do, walk from Capital Interchange Way up Lionel Road South and join the same queue as home fans. Gunnersbury station does not open until an hour after the final whistle and queues are likely. Taxis take longer after the game. Last-train times: not stated.
tips: The stadium is fully cashless (contactless, Apple Pay, Google Pay; chip and PIN over £45). Arrive early - turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off and searches are thorough. Early Bird prices in the away kiosks for the first 30 minutes after opening (£4 draught beer, £4 pies); alcohol may be withdrawn for high-risk fixtures. Report issues by texting BFC plus your message to 62277. For ticket problems on the day go to the stadium Box Office before entering.

arrival: Nottingham railway station is roughly a 20-minute walk (about 1.4 miles) or a 10-minute bus ride from the City Ground; from the city centre it is a brisk 15-20 minute walk - follow signs for Trent Bridge Cricket Ground, over the River Trent. Nottingham City Transport buses 5-11 drop closest to the ground but are heavily congested on matchdays. The nearest tram stop is Meadows Embankment, then a 20-minute walk. Taxi ranks are on Station Street and Queens Road at the front and rear of the station, or use Uber or Bolt.
from_airport: Not stated by the sources. (East Midlands Airport is the nearest, with the Skylink bus into Nottingham - unverified.)
away_end: Away fans are in the Bridgford Stand (lower Bridgford Block W is safe standing). Enter via the turnstile printed on your digital ticket - away turnstiles are in the range 41-53 behind the Bridgford Stand, next to the Visitors' Ticket Office. Turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off; most close 10 minutes after kick-off, a few stay open for late-comers. No re-entry.
meeting: The Nest (Iremonger Road, NG2 3HU, next to Notts County's Meadow Lane) is Nottingham's dedicated away-fan fanzone, about a 10-minute walk from the away turnstiles and on the direct walking route from the station, with capacity for over 1300, big screen, bars and street food; it opens only to away ticket holders on selected matchdays (free tickets may be required) - see nestnotts.co.uk. No pubs are named by the sources.
bags: Only small bags smaller than A4 (21cm x 29.7cm) are allowed; no large bags, suitcases, laptop bags or rucksacks, and Forest state they have nowhere to hold large bags and there is no bag drop. Clear plastic bottles up to 500ml, small compact cameras and small fold-up umbrellas are allowed; banned items include alcohol, cans and glass, food, face coverings, drones, poles and selfie sticks, musical instruments and video recording equipment. Banners need prior permission from Stadium Operations (0115 982 4444).
after: It is a 20-minute walk back to Nottingham station, or buses 5-11 (expect congestion). Queue details and last-train times to Manchester or London: not stated.
tips: The City Ground is cashless (card payments only). All tickets are digital for 2026/27 - have your phone charged with brightness up and the QR code ready; if there is a problem, the Visitors' Ticket Office Collection Point next to the away turnstiles opens 90 minutes before kick-off (proof of booking and photo ID required) and closes at half-time. Parking at the ground is very limited; use the approved car parks at Meadow Lane, Cattlemarket, Lady Bay Sports Ground or County Hall and avoid West Bridgford residential streets. Under-14s must be with an adult. Report anti-social behaviour by texting FOREST to 80800.

arrival: Sunderland railway station is the nearest main-line station, 10-15 minutes' walk from the ground (just under a mile, north along the riverbank). The Tyne and Wear Metro serves the ground via two stops: St Peter's (3 minutes' walk) and Stadium of Light (10 minutes' walk, deceptively named). Buses E2, 2, 3, 4, 9, 12, 13, 15, 16, 23, 24 and 56 stop nearby and Park Lane Interchange bus station is within walking distance; a free Park and Ride runs from Sunderland Enterprise Park off the A1231 every five minutes for 90 minutes before kick-off. Taxi drop-off is outside the Black Cat House store any time before kick-off.
from_airport: Newcastle International Airport is roughly a 40-minute drive; the Metro runs direct from the airport to Stadium of Light station in about 45 minutes to an hour.
away_end: Away fans are in the upper tier of the North Stand, entering through turnstiles 69-74, which open 90 minutes before kick-off. Fans needing lift access should go to the 76 Yards entrance and ask stewards for the lift to level 3. Standard away allocation is around 3000.
meeting: The club's guide directs visiting fans to pubs around Keel Square and High Street West in the city centre (then over the Keel Crossing footbridge to the ground), Sheepfolds Stables street food and bars on the route, the Fans Museum between Roker and the stadium (open to away fans, serves drinks), and pubs along Roker seafront; the Beacon of Light Fanzone next to the stadium is open to both sets of fans from two and a half hours before kick-off. Football Ground Guide names Greens, Streetbar SR1, The Albion, The Wheatsheaf and The Avenue as away-friendly.
bags: Only small bags smaller than A4 are allowed; banned items include alcohol and canned drinks, glass and plastic bottles, sports bottles and flasks, laptops and tablets, large cameras, large umbrellas, poles, air horns, musical instruments, fireworks, flares and buggies. There is no left-luggage facility; for selected fixtures an advanced search bans coins, vapes, power banks and umbrellas, with a steward collection-ticket scheme for vapes, power banks and umbrellas only.
after: After the match, Metro passengers heading north towards Newcastle must board at Stadium of Light station, while those heading south must board at St Peter's. Expect heavy traffic and a residents-only parking scheme nearby; the Park and Ride buses continue running after the game. Last trains to Manchester or London: not stated.
tips: The Stadium of Light is cashless, card only; the away concourse has two food and drink courtyards open from turnstiles opening, at half time and for 30 minutes after full time. Strict no re-admission. Supporter Liaison Officer: chris.waters@safc.com; asksafc.com handles pre-match queries.

arrival: Metrolink tram from the city centre (Piccadilly, Victoria, Market Street, St Peter's Square or Piccadilly Gardens) to the Etihad Campus stop takes 10-15 minutes (about 8 minutes from Piccadilly), every six minutes Monday to Saturday; Etihad Campus is in Zone 2, contactless tap-in accepted. The club says the walk from the city centre is roughly 30 minutes along the signposted Citylink walking route from Piccadilly through Ancoats, New Islington and Holt Town (20-25 minutes via Great Ancoats Street, Pollard Street and Ashton New Road). Ashburys rail station is five minutes by train from Piccadilly then about a 20-minute walk. TfGM runs matchday bus routes from across Greater Manchester.
from_airport: Not stated by the club pages. (Manchester Airport is on the Metrolink network: tram or train to the city centre, then the Etihad Campus tram - unverified.)
away_end: Away fans are in the South Stand (right-hand side behind the goal, across three tiers) and should use entrances L1, L2 and L3, which open two hours before kick-off; the first two tiers are preferred for the view. Away coaches park in the Grey Car Park opposite the away turnstiles.
meeting: The club names no away pubs and says local pubs are used by home supporters; drinking in public areas is not allowed across Greater Manchester. Football Ground Guide says most away fans drink in the city centre and take the tram out, lists The Townley, Grove Inn and The Corner Shop as City pubs where colours should not be worn, says Mary D's should be avoided, and specifically tells Manchester United fans to use the city centre.
bags: Only small handheld bags no larger than A4 (12 x 8 x 3 inches) are accepted; backpacks, holdalls and rucksacks are refused regardless of size, and pyrotechnics and smoke bombs are banned. There are no lockers, but a bag drop operates in the Grey car park inside the away compound at £10 per item.
after: Away fans may be held back briefly after the final whistle while nearby areas clear, by agreement with Greater Manchester Police, with PA announcements. Tram queues at Etihad Campus can be up to 30 minutes and many fans prefer the 25-30 minute walk back to Piccadilly along the A662; TfGM also runs post-match shuttle buses. Last trains to London: not stated.
tips: Arrive no later than 60 minutes before kick-off; expect at least two search and ticket-check points on the approach. The Etihad is cashless. Pre-arranged ticket collections are at the South Stand Ticket Office from two hours before kick-off with photo ID, and tickets are not reprinted on the day, so arrange collection through United; download mobile tickets before arriving. No re-admission; under-14s must be with an adult.

arrival: The ground is just under 10 minutes' walk from Ipswich railway station (about a quarter of a mile: straight over the bridge from the station, right at the Royal Mail sorting office). The town centre is less than 10 minutes' walk away. Trains run from London Liverpool Street (Greater Anglia, 2-3 an hour, about 70 minutes on faster services) and hourly from Peterborough with short 4-coach trains that get very busy. A London Road Park and Ride bus stops a short walk from the stadium.
from_airport: Not stated by the club guide. (London Stansted is the nearest practical airport: train via Cambridge, or coach/train via London - unverified.)
away_end: Away fans are in the Cobbold Stand, in blocks VU1, VU2 and VU3 (safe standing, upper tier) and VL and VA (seated); buy a seated ticket if you cannot stand for long periods, and there is no lift to the upper tier. Away turnstiles are 10/11, 12/13 and 14/15/16/17, with the away accessible entrance alongside; turnstiles open 90 minutes before daytime kick-offs and 75 minutes before evening games.
meeting: The club names The Station Hotel opposite the railway station as the official away pub (garden, TV screens, Greene King beers); most pubs around the ground are home only and the Portman Road FanZone is home fans only. For those arriving via the A14 the club lists The Maltings in Stowmarket, the Sorrel Horse in Barham and the Live Lounge in Stowmarket as away-friendly. Football Ground Guide also names the Lord Nelson, Dove Street Inn and Isaacs on the Quay.
bags: No bags larger than A4 are permitted and there are no facilities to leave bags at the stadium (Football Ground Guide quotes a maximum of 30 x 20 x 10 cm and mentions an external paid storage option in Alderman Park). Musical instruments and selfie sticks are banned in the away end; flags need a fire certificate.
after: After evening games the trains back to London are limited, usually 22:23 and 22:43, and there are no post-match options at all on the Peterborough line after evening matches. The Portman Road car park exit is closed for 15-20 minutes after the game while pedestrians clear and nearby roads take at least an hour to clear. Last trains to Manchester: not stated.
tips: All away fixtures are all-ticket with no sales on the day; the away ticket collection window is next to the away turnstiles. Portman Road is cashless, including programmes (sold only outside the ground). Allow at least an extra hour for train travel because of frequent weekend engineering works, and check the club's match-specific guide sent to United about two weeks before the game; no re-admission.

arrival: The arena is about 4 miles north of Coventry railway station (15-20 minutes by road), so it is not walkable from town. The club-subsidised shuttle bus costs £5 return (contactless only, no one-way tickets), picking up at the rail replacement stop by Coventry station (near Central Six) and White Street Coach Park, from three hours before kick-off at half-hour intervals until one hour before, dropping at the bus station at Arena Park shopping centre. Coventry Arena station is on site but has no special matchday service and only takes short trains. By public bus: No. 9 from the station to the Transport Museum, then No. 3 from Trinity Street or No. 5 from Pool Meadow to Arena Park (Tesco) and through the underpass. A taxi from the centre is around £15.
from_airport: Birmingham International Airport is the nearest, a short train ride or drive from Coventry (Coventry is about 10 minutes by train from Birmingham International).
away_end: Away fans are in the South Stand, usually blocks 6-9, with safe standing in blocks 6 and 7 and a wheelchair platform at the front of block 8 accessed via Gate 25; the South Stand is not connected to the other stands. Specific turnstile numbers are shown on your ticket; turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off and the away late turnstile is number 5.
meeting: The club recommends The Longford Engine, 270 Bedworth Road, CV6 6BP, a 17-minute walk from the arena. Football Ground Guide adds the Bull and Anchor (Wheelwright Lane, about 10 minutes), The Old Crown, Byatts Brewery and Dhillon's Brewery. Options around the ground are limited, so drinking in the city centre before travelling out is the usual choice.
bags: The arena's prohibited items list bans large bags and suitcases but gives no size limit; also banned are glasses, bottles and cans, outside food and drink, cameras, computer tablets, long umbrellas, flagpoles, selfie sticks, air horns, fireworks and flares, baby buggies and prams, and flags over 2m x 1m. Bags may be searched on entry; no locker or left-luggage option is stated.
after: After the game, segregation means away fans cannot turn left towards Arena Shopping Park; you are directed across Car Park B (where away coaches park) and left at the exit gate to reach the shopping park and the train station. The A444 Jimmy Hill Way is closed for a short period after every match. Shuttle buses back to the city centre leave Arena Park from two hours after kick-off at half-hour intervals (for a 3pm game 17:00 to 18:30); expect station queues and gridlocked roads. Last trains to Manchester or London: not stated.
tips: All South Stand kiosks and the club shop are cashless. Have your barcode ticket ready for the scanners and allow time for searches; arriving 15 minutes before kick-off means queuing. No re-admission; a half-time smoking area is outside the South Stand; drums are not allowed in the away end and flags need prior approval via safety@ccfc.co.uk. Car Park C is the closest paid parking to the South Stand.

arrival: Pokesdown for Boscombe is the nearest station, about a 15-minute walk (turn right onto Christchurch Road, then right into Gloucester Road); Pokesdown is not currently wheelchair accessible. Bournemouth (Central) station is a 25 to 30-minute walk: leave by the south exit, turn left to Holdenhurst Road, follow it to the Queens Park roundabout and turn right into Kings Park Drive. Yellow Buses No. 33 runs from outside Bournemouth station south exit (ask for Kings Park Drive), or take a taxi from either station. The club discourages driving: from 2026/27 there is no general admission parking in the Kings Park car parks and the council enforces local restrictions on matchdays.
from_airport: Not stated by the club. (Bournemouth Airport is 15 minutes away by taxi; from London airports, the train to Bournemouth or Pokesdown - unverified.)
away_end: Away fans are in the Vitality East Stand, blocks 21 to 24, in one corner of the stand, entered via Turnstile F; there is an away-accessible entrance next to the away turnstiles. Turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off.
meeting: Mello Mello Bar (677 Christchurch Road, Boscombe) is on the walking route from Pokesdown and welcomes visiting fans; Football Ground Guide also lists the Bell Inn (915 Christchurch Road, Pokesdown) and The George Tapps (Old Christchurch Road, town centre). The 1910 Supporters Bar and Queens Park Hotel are home-only.
bags: Bags must be no bigger than A4 and all bags are searched; the club advises not bringing one unless necessary. Banned items include alcohol, cans, glass and flasks, air horns, lasers, pyrotechnics, umbrellas, large bags or cabin bags, large-lens cameras, selfie sticks and flags over 2m x 1m (flags need a fire certificate and no poles). No bag storage is mentioned.
after: Traffic around the ground is heavy after the game; allow 20 to 45 minutes to clear the area, or walk back to Boscombe/Pokesdown (about 15 minutes) or take a bus to Bournemouth Square. Last train times to London or Manchester: not stated; post-match journeys are much longer on engineering-work weekends, so check your route.
tips: The stadium is cashless. Only travel with a valid ticket; no upgrades on the day, and bring photo ID to collect a pre-arranged duplicate from the main ticket office. Food and drink are served in the away section; redevelopment works around the ground mean you should allow extra time and follow stewards.

arrival: Four stations serve the ground: White Hart Lane (Overground from Liverpool Street, about 5 minutes' walk), Northumberland Park (Greater Anglia from Liverpool Street and Stratford, about 10 minutes, and the station the club steers away fans towards; the away entrances are on Worcester Avenue via Park Lane), Tottenham Hale (Victoria line plus Greater Anglia, about 25 minutes) and Seven Sisters (Victoria line and Overground, about 30 minutes, no step-free access). The Victoria line is very crowded before weeknight games and trains sometimes skip Seven Sisters. Buses 149, 249, 279 and 349 run up the High Road, though routes are diverted by road closures. Taxis cannot drop off near the stadium; arrange a point at least 15 minutes' walk away.
from_airport: Northumberland Park is served by Greater Anglia trains from Stansted Airport (via the Liverpool Street line). Other airports: not stated by the club.
away_end: Visiting supporters are in Blocks 114 to 118 in the north-east corner, lower tier (Block 234 for accessible seating). Approach via Worcester Avenue and use Entrances 11 and 12 (11a is the accessible entrance); there is a security cordon, metal detector and pat-down before the ticket turnstiles.
meeting: Most pubs near the stadium are home-only with doormen. Football Ground Guide names the Antwerp Arms (Church Road, mixed home and away) and the brewery taprooms on the Compass Industrial Estate (Tottenham Brewing Co, Tariff Road; One Mile End, Redemption and Bohem on West Road), 5 to 10 minutes from the away turnstiles, and suggests drinking in central London, e.g. the Hamilton Hall Wetherspoon at Liverpool Street.
bags: The club strongly advises against bringing a bag; if you must, it has to be a clear carrier bag up to 30cm x 30cm or a personal bag no larger than A4 (21cm x 30cm); laptop sleeves up to 37cm x 31cm. Expect longer queues with a bag and airport-style searches. No bag drop or storage is provided.
after: Post-match queuing systems run at all four stations; follow signage and stewards. Trains at Northumberland Park are split into northbound and southbound queues and the station gets very congested; some fans walk to Seven Sisters or Tottenham Hale for the Victoria line. Last train times: not stated; use the toilets inside the ground as there are none at the local stations.
tips: The stadium and campus are fully cashless. The stadium opens two hours before kick-off; arriving early avoids peak transport and security queues. Touchline Grills and Tap Inns in the visitors' section open two hours before kick-off; every attendee, including babes in arms, needs a ticket. For United's 23 May visit the trips page assumes a day trip via Stansted - the 06:00 Ryanair out and an evening flight home.

arrival: The nearest tube is Fulham Broadway (District line, Wimbledon branch; change at Earl's Court if needed), 5 to 10 minutes' walk; it is step-free with lifts. West Brompton and Imperial Wharf (Overground, between Clapham Junction and Willesden Junction) are about 15 minutes' walk. Buses 14, 211 and 414 stop outside on Fulham Road. Fulham Road between Harwood Road and Hortensia Road closes 90 minutes before kick-off until about an hour after; parking is residents-only, so the club advises public transport.
from_airport: Not stated by the club. (Heathrow: Piccadilly line to Earl's Court then District line to Fulham Broadway - unverified.)
away_end: Away fans are in the Shed End (South Stand), split across Shed Lower and Shed Upper, on the right-hand side as you face the stand; both are safe-standing rail-seat areas. The ticket office behind the Shed End next to the Megastore handles away enquiries. Entry readers open about 90 minutes before kick-off; the club does not publish turnstile letters.
meeting: The club states none of the pubs around Stamford Bridge admit visiting fans and that the nearest away-friendly pubs are in Earl's Court, about 25 to 30 minutes' walk (1.4 miles). Football Ground Guide names The Courtfield Tavern (opposite Earl's Court station), The Goose (248 North End Road), The Blackbird and Earl's Court Tavern (Earls Court Road).
bags: Only bags no larger than A4 (maximum 30cm x 20cm x 10cm) are allowed and all are searched; the club provides no bag storage but points to an independent matchday bag drop at Fulham Broadway Shopping Centre. Prohibited items include prams, large-lens cameras, glass, cans, plastic bottles over 500ml, aerosols, flag poles, umbrellas, selfie sticks, air horns and musical instruments; no smoking or vaping.
after: Fulham Broadway is very crowded after the game and its entrance has been closed at full time; wait a few minutes or walk to Earl's Court, West Kensington, West Brompton, Gloucester Road or South Kensington instead. Last train times to Manchester: not stated.
tips: Stamford Bridge is cashless. Under-16s must be accompanied by an adult. The club encourages arriving early and eating and drinking inside the ground; there is strictly no re-admittance.

arrival: The stadium is about 7km north of the centre. Visiting clubs (Tottenham 2022, Arsenal 2024) tell away fans to take the Green (Verde) metro line from Rossio/Baixa to Telheiras, about 15 minutes, then walk roughly 10 minutes to the away gate under police direction; both stations are step-free. Do not get off at Campo Grande, which is next to the stadium but reserved for home fans and described as strictly forbidden for away supporters. Fans are also advised to stay in the city centre and avoid the stadium area until travelling to the match.
from_airport: Lisbon Airport is on the metro network (Red line); change onto the Green line for Telheiras rather than using Campo Grande. A taxi or Uber is the alternative.
away_end: At Tottenham's 2022 visit the away section was on two levels: level 0 blocks A9 and A11 (turnstile A) and level 4 blocks B7, B9, B11 and B13 (turnstile B), reached via Gate 1 with safety netting across the whole visiting area; you cannot move between levels. The standard UEFA allocation is around 2,500 and United's own travel guide will confirm the gate. Turnstiles open two hours before kick-off.
meeting: Rossio Square and the surrounding streets in the centre are the usual base for away fans. Football Ground Guide lists bars such as The Red Frog Speakeasy, Artis Bar and Clube da Esquina, and sports bars The Couch, Alta Spot and Mignon; none are specifically away-fan pubs.
bags: Bags up to A4 size (20cm x 30cm) are admitted after a search; there is no bag storage. Alcohol, bottles, cans, food, flagpoles, umbrellas, radios and footballs are banned; power banks are allowed; poleless flags up to 1m x 1m need a fire certificate. No alcohol is sold in general admission areas.
after: Away fans are held back for roughly 15 to 30 minutes after the final whistle until police release them; toilets and kiosks stay open. Return to the centre on the Green line from Telheiras, or stay on the away side of the stadium for taxis or Uber. Last metro times: not stated (the Lisbon metro normally runs until about 01:00 - unverified).
tips: Tickets are digital/print-at-home and sent to the lead booker about five days before the game; download them before you set off and do not travel without one. Aim to be at the gate at least an hour before kick-off. Kiosks were card-only at Arsenal's visit; watch for pickpockets and keep passport and cash separate.

arrival: The stadium is in the town itself, about 10 minutes' walk north of the centre. Vila-real station is on the Renfe Cercanías C-6 line between València Nord and Castelló: around 50 to 60 minutes from Valencia and 10 to 20 minutes from Castellón, with several trains an hour off-peak; the walk from the station to the ground is flat and takes 15 to 20 minutes. Most away fans stay in Valencia or Castellón because hotels in Vila-real are very limited. UK government advice for United's 2021 visit quoted taxis at about EUR 80 to Valencia and EUR 20 to Castellón.
from_airport: Valencia Airport (VLC), about 70km south, is the practical gateway: metro into Valencia then Cercanías C-6 to Vila-real, roughly an hour from the city. The trips page notes no direct CPH flight that week (one stop via Amsterdam).
away_end: Away fans are in the upper tier of the Fondo Norte (North Stand) behind the goal, a steep tier used exclusively for visitors; allocations are small (around 1,100-1,200 is typical). For United's 2021 visit the entry point was Gate 25; the away gate is confirmed by United per fixture, with ID and bag checks at several cordons.
meeting: No away-fan pubs are named. Football Ground Guide lists 1800 Cocktail Bar, Vila-Beer Irish Bar and Bar el Belga in the town; Les Porches near Plaça de la Vila is where fans of both sides gather before kick-off.
bags: No formal size limit is published. Spanish law (Law 19/2007, cited by the club) bans weapons, flares, fireworks, flammable or smoke-producing items and offensive banners; 2021 advice to United fans also barred alcohol, cans, glass, bottle tops and containers over 0.5 litres. No bag storage is mentioned at the ground.
after: Visiting fans are usually held in the stadium for 20 to 30 minutes after the final whistle. For a 21:00 kick-off Manchester City's 2025/26 guide warned that public transport from Villarreal stops at 22:00 local time, so there are no trains or buses after the game and only a few taxis; pre-book coaches or taxis back to Valencia or Castellón. For daytime games the Cercanías platform fills quickly after the whistle, so buy a return ticket on arrival.
tips: Carry photo ID (passport) with your ticket; checks happen at police cordons and turnstiles. Gates open 90 minutes to two hours before kick-off; arrive early for the security checks. Tickets are print-at-home, personal and non-transferable, sent about five days before the match; do not book travel until you have one, as kick-off times can change.
